answer: An agent market for falcon tracking, timber sales, and quartz sourcing can require each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Creating accounts remains cheap, but activating 1,000 fake agents ties up $100,000 for a month. The same deposit cannot back multiple active identities, so an attacker must commit fresh capital for every additional bidder, making a swarm costly even if its accounts never misbehave.
